# pengdows.efcore.conformance

> Black-box conformance tests for relational providers of Entity Framework Core 10.

## Purpose

This repository tests externally observable behavior through documented EF Core public APIs. The provider is configured through an adapter, operations run through `DbContext`, LINQ, and EF Core relational APIs, and results are asserted through fresh contexts or documented public state.

## Boundary

- Do not inspect generated SQL, EF provider services, EF internals, or provider implementation types in shared tests.
- Keep provider setup and database provisioning in `IProviderAdapter` implementations.
- Capabilities declare applicability only. They never alter expected values or assertions.
- Strict runs require a supported or unsupported declaration for every feature in `ProviderCapabilities.KnownFeatures`.
- ADO.NET `DataTypes` metadata is the preferred native type inventory. Mark catalog evidence independent only when it is independent of the EF model. Types read from test-created tables are `SELF_DERIVED` and excluded from coverage totals.
- Run the same test assembly against one provider per process. Compare report JSON with the runner's `--compare` command.

## Project map

- `src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Contracts/`: adapter contracts, capabilities, type discovery, and outcomes.
- `src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Runner/`: adapter loading, test execution, JSON/JUnit reports, type discovery, and cross-provider comparison.
- `src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Inventory/`: reflection-generated EF Core public API inventory.
- `tests/pengdows.efcore.conformance.EF10.Relational/`: shared EF Core 10 relational behavioral tests.
- `adapters/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.MicrosoftSqlite/`: Microsoft provider reference adapter; included in the standalone solution.
- `adapters/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.PengdowsSqlite/`: pengdows adapter; depends on the separate pengdows ADO.NET repository and is intentionally outside the solution build.
- `manifests/`: EF Core 10 contract and generated API inventory.

## Build and run

```sh
dotnet build pengdows.efcore.conformance.slnx
export PENGDOWS_EFCORE_CONFORMANCE_CONNECTION_STRING='Data Source=/tmp/efcore-reference.db'
dotnet run --project src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Runner -- --run \
  tests/pengdows.efcore.conformance.EF10.Relational/pengdows.efcore.conformance.EF10.Relational.csproj \
  "$PWD/adapters/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.MicrosoftSqlite/bin/Debug/net10.0/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.MicrosoftSqlite.dll" \
  pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.MicrosoftSqlite.MicrosoftSqliteAdapter /tmp/efcore-reference-report
```

Run the same test assembly for another provider with a separate disposable database and report directory. Compare results:

```sh
dotnet run --project src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Runner -- --compare \
  /tmp/candidate-report/conformance-results.json \
  /tmp/efcore-reference-report/conformance-results.json \
  /tmp/provider-comparison.json
```

Append `--cleanup-database` to `--run` only when the configured database is dedicated and disposable. The runner then calls the adapter cleanup hook after writing test results.

## Provider configuration

The sibling ADO.NET conformance project uses `providers/*.json` profiles to describe driver, target, connection string, environment, dialect, and type inventory. The EF Core harness borrows declarative per-provider profiles for adapter selection and connection strings: `profiles/*.json` names a compiled adapter assembly/type and a connection string template with `${ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE}` placeholders. Run one with `--run-profile <profile.json> <test-project> <report-directory> [--cleanup-database]`. Adapter assembly paths are relative to the profile file unless absolute.

EF profiles deliberately leave EF provider configuration, capabilities, database initialization, and cleanup in `IProviderAdapter`. A profile cannot change expectations or assertions. Profiles do not provision containers or remote databases; infrastructure setup remains external. The old direct `--run` form and `PENGDOWS_EFCORE_CONFORMANCE_CONNECTION_STRING` are still supported.

## Current status

- EF Core baseline: 10.0.14 on `net10.0`.
- The public API inventory is generated from the Core, Abstractions, and Relational assemblies. Disposition rules in `manifests/efcore-10.json` attach rationales to EF-owned and provider-service surfaces; tests override those rules. Current counts: 615 overload entries in tested API families, 131 uncovered member families, 204 entries awaiting classification, 4,051 EF-owned entries, and 7,710 provider-service or model-configuration entries marked not directly applicable.
- Latest comparable full SQLite runs execute 281 cases each: 271 pass on both; 5 decimal fidelity cases fail only on pengdows SQLite; 5 cases fail on both SQLite providers. Shared failures are async negative `ElementAt`, both `RightJoin` unmatched-row cases, and both TPT affected-entry-count cases. Shared failures are not automatically attributed to EF Core. Both providers pass keyless `[Keyless]` entity materialization through parameterized `FromSqlInterpolated` in sync and async paths, shadow-property filtering through `EF.Property` and predicate evaluation through `EF.Constant`/`EF.Parameter`, and escaped wildcard matching through `EF.Functions.Like` and parameterized `EF.CompileQuery`/`EF.CompileAsyncQuery` on sync/async paths, boundary round-trips for CLR date, time, boolean, binary, and converted enum values, sync/async store-generated integer keys, pre-canceled async query and SaveChanges operations, sync/async SaveChanges behavior with automatic change detection disabled, context-wide sync/async `QueryTrackingBehavior`, sync/async snapshot and notification change-tracking strategies, `SaveChanges(false)` state retention followed by `AcceptAllChanges`, and changes with snapshot detection disabled, sync/async `WarningBehavior` handling for `Log`, `Ignore`, and `Throw`, sync/async materialization under all supported `PropertyAccessMode` values, `TrackGraph`, deferred `CascadeChanges`, sync/async nested complex-value updates, sync/async optimistic concurrency conflict recovery, sync/async DI-created `IDbContextFactory` contexts and scoped `AddDbContext` contexts, savepoint release and transaction interface checks, database facade provider/transaction/savepoint configuration cases, `DatabaseFacade` commit/rollback methods, `PropertyValues.SetValues` and snapshot helpers, direct `EntityEntry.DetectChanges`, `DbContext` success and failure events, `DbSet` convenience and async enumerator cases, `AsTracking` overrides, sync and async query `Load`, context disposal and owned-connection closure, `IgnoreAutoIncludes`, async `ForEachAsync` and array/set/dictionary materializers, direct `DbContext` add/attach/update/remove and range operations, current-database-value checks for tracked entities, explicit collection/reference loading, migration discovery/application including table rename, raw SQL migration operations, and rollback/reapply, migration-created foreign key, unique constraint, and check constraint enforcement, keyless `[Keyless]` raw SQL materialization, sync/async `Cascade`, `SetNull`, `ClientCascade`, `ClientSetNull`, `NoAction`, and `ClientNoAction` delete behavior, `[EntityTypeConfiguration]`/`IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` and `[Owned]` attribute-driven model mappings, getter-only property persistence through `[BackingField]`, filtered unique index behavior controlled by the declared `filtered-indexes` capability, nested owned-to-JSON persistence and property queries controlled by `json-mapping`, unique index enforcement from `[Index]`, built-in function translation from `[DbFunction]`, nullable function result preservation on sync and async paths, precision attribute value fidelity, database deletion/recreation checks, and pending-model-change checks, external ADO.NET transaction cases, external connection replacement, scalar `SqlQueryRaw<T>` cases, generic `DbContext.Find`/`FindAsync` cases, database facade configuration cases, warning configuration, and `ExecuteSql`/`ExecuteSqlAsync` command cases.
- SQLite ADO.NET providers do not advertise `DataTypes`. Supplemental types discovered from test-created schema are self-derived; independent native type coverage is not currently established.
- The test suite is a growing conformance slice, not yet complete coverage of every applicable EF Core public API. Consult `README.md`, `manifests/efcore-10.json`, and `manifests/efcore-10-api-inventory.json` for disposition rules, current counts, rationales, and uncovered members.


## Unfinished work

Inventory dimensions overlap: unclassified entries can belong to uncovered member families and must not be summed.

1. Classify all 204 `unclassified` entries with a reason or behavioral test. The largest cluster is `MigrationBuilder` (31 entries), followed by relational builder extensions and capability enums.
2. Add behavioral contracts for the 131 uncovered public API member families. Cover each observable provider responsibility, including separate sync and async paths where both APIs exist. An inventory link alone does not cover all overloads or scenarios.
3. Triage the five pengdows-only decimal fidelity failures. Investigate the five failures reproduced by both SQLite providers (async negative `ElementAt`, sync/async unmatched `RightJoin`, sync/async TPT save counts) against documented contracts and additional providers. Reproduction on the reference provider is evidence, not proof of an EF Core defect.
4. Establish independent database type discovery. SQLite does not expose ADO.NET `DataTypes`, and the current supplemental type list comes from test-created schema. Compare ADO.NET metadata with an independent database catalog, record discrepancies, and test each discovered type's mapping and value fidelity.
5. Run against additional relational providers and server versions while keeping shared expectations provider-independent and capability declarations explicit.
6. Add a separate EF Core 11 target after its release contract is established; generate its inventory from its actual assemblies and add version-specific tests for changed or new behavior.

EF Core 10 completion requires zero unclassified entries, behavioral or justified disposition for each applicable public API family, sync/async coverage where both APIs exist, independently discovered native-type coverage, triaged failures, and reports that distinguish pass, fail, unsupported, infrastructure error, and uncovered work. The current 281-case two-SQLite comparison is an initial slice, not completion.
